Russian profanity data sources and transformations

1. safetext by DeepSafe, MIT license, copyright (c) 2023 DeepSafe.
   https://github.com/viddexa/safetext
   Commit afe96c8053e577e7e1e3a2eb5c9503ac157efbb5
   Input safetext/languages/ru/words.txt
   Filtered to reviewed obscene families, deduplicated and folded to lowercase.
   Medical terms and neutral entries from the aggregate are excluded.
   Full MIT notice: MIT-safetext.txt.

2. OpenCorpora Russian dictionary, CC BY-SA 3.0.
   https://opencorpora.org/dict.php
   License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/legalcode
   Accessed through pymorphy3-dicts-ru 2.4.417150.4580142 and pymorphy3 2.0.6.
   Known word inflections matching the selected obscene families were extracted;
   model-guessed parses were not used. Runtime needs no morphology package.

The expanded badwords_exact.txt data including extracted inflections is
redistributed under CC BY-SA 3.0 (license URI above). Existing entries retained.
The data license does not change the license for the bot source code.
Rebuild: install pymorphy3==2.0.6 in a build environment, then run
python tools/build_badwords.py /path/to/safetext/languages/ru/words.txt
